writer.recovery: A lock file is not a lock. `flock` lives on the open file description, so the kernel drops it when the holder exits for any reason - clean stop, crash, SIGKILL - and the next writer acquires immediately. There is therefore no stale-lock timeout and no break-the-lock path: a lock file naming a dead pid is read as a hint and overwritten in place by whoever next acquires it, and this writer never removes or replaces another process's lock file. The one case the lock alone cannot cover is the file being deleted or replaced underneath a live holder, because the replacement is a different inode and locks cleanly; the holder therefore re-checks the inode before every append and stops writing when it can no longer prove it owns the root.

basis.formula: basis = mark - index; premium_pct = (mark - index) / index * 100
